baseline_models.focus_anchor: Focus words 1, 3-5, and 7: intention, causative substitution, the parents' Lord, comparative good, and zakah.
baseline_models.mechanism: An intended substitute enters the lost child's place, but the Lord-title makes replacement an act of nurture and completion. Good is specified through zakah, so the comparison measures a developing combination of increase and purification rather than generic superiority.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate will supplies the initiating intention behind the replacement.
One entity occupying another's place supplies literal substitution.
Nurture, repair, and completion make the Lord the cultivator of the new trajectory.
Beneficial good constrains 'better' to a positively functioning outcome.
Growth and increase turn zakah into a developmental measure.
Purity and soundness add an ethical measure that coexists with growth.

changed_reading.before: A better child will simply compensate the two parents.
changed_reading.after: The intended substitute is better as a Lord-tended trajectory whose operative measures are beneficial growth and purification.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Focus words 7-9: suitability, comparative nearness, and ruhm.
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing comparison doubles relational language: nearness can be kin proximity, while ruhm can be mercy, kinship, and the womb. The desired better is therefore fitted to the two parents' family bond, not merely an isolated individual possessing more compassion.

activation_trace.role: Suitability makes zakah a measure of fit with the parents' condition.
Kin and lineage proximity gives the comparative a specifically familial axis.
Close kinship makes mercy a reciprocal family relation rather than a one-way feeling.
The womb supplies the generative site through which replacement rejoins the family.

changed_reading.before: The replacement will be more compassionate toward the parents.
changed_reading.after: The replacement will be more closely fitted into womb, lineage, and reciprocal family attachment, with mercy functioning as relational nearness as well as emotion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The journey advances by overshooting, returning along an earlier trace, receiving specially given knowledge, and admitting failure to encompass an event's interior. Later explanation returns deeds to their outcomes. The focus comparison therefore operates at an outcome level disclosed after the destructive appearance, not at the level of immediate visibility.

activation_trace.role: Beneficial good is the focus predicate whose time horizon is being revised.
Return to a prior place makes backward movement the route to recognition.
Following a prior trace supplies the evidentiary path by which missed meaning is recovered.
Disclosure to a knower supplies privileged access to what the events mean.
Complete cognitive enclosure names precisely what the observer lacks.
Return to an eventual outcome makes retrospective explanation the interpretive frame.

structural_cues: 18:61-64 places recognition after overshooting and literal retracing; 18:71-78 repeatedly orders deed, objection, and only then explanation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies missed and retraced signs, specially given knowledge, non-encompassment, and later outcome-explanation; I infer an arrow from delayed knowledge to the time horizon of 'better.' A live alternative is that these cues govern only the learner's understanding, not the comparison itself.

changed_reading.before: The replacement is visibly better at the moment of the loss.
changed_reading.after: The replacement is named better from a disclosed future outcome that the immediate observer cannot yet encompass.

context_deltas.mechanism: The vessel episode opposes a bounded defect to total coerced confiscation. That pattern activates substitution as preemptive preservation: local loss or impairment can protect vulnerable owners from a larger loss, so the focus good names the preserved family outcome rather than a painless process.

activation_trace.role: Literal substitution anchors the protective-loss analogy in the focus.
Beneficial good shifts evaluation from the damaged part to the preserved whole.
A localized breach supplies the bounded intervention that appears destructive.
Seizure supplies the larger dispossession that the defect averts.
Total inclusion turns the threatened taking into an engulfing loss.
Coercive unjust taking identifies the destructive system from which the owners are preserved.

structural_cues: 18:71 presents the breach as ruinous, while 18:79 places the workers' retained but impaired vessel against a ruler's taking of every vessel by force.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies local damage, vulnerable workers, and universal forced seizure; I infer that bounded harm preserves against total harm and carry that mechanism into the focus replacement. The live alternative is that this preservation logic is confined to property and should not be transferred to a person.

changed_reading.before: Replacement is compensation after an isolated loss.
changed_reading.after: Replacement participates in a preemptive preservation pattern in which a bounded loss averts a more engulfing family loss.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same Z-K-W inventory marks the killed living self as pure and specifies the requested replacement by zakah. Youth and the feared future pressure on believing parents force a distinction between present status and prospective relational trajectory. The focus comparison can evaluate unfolding growth without retroactively turning the protest's pure self into concealed guilt.

activation_trace.role: Growth makes the focus zakah prospective and developmental.
Present purity preserves the force of the observer's protest instead of erasing it.
The living self keeps the event's immediate moral cost fully in view.
Youth supplies an unfinished life stage from which a later trajectory is projected.
Settled belief identifies the parental state exposed to future pressure.
Overtaking and overpowering make the feared harm relationally imposed on both parents.
Crossing a limit supplies the projected direction of the pressure.
Veiling truth names the feared endpoint for the parents' settled belief.

structural_cues: 18:74 predicates purity of the killed self; 18:80 shifts to a feared effect on two believing parents; 18:81 compares a replacement for those same two.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies present purity, youth, and projected parental overpowering; I infer a snapshot-to-trajectory distinction and assign the comparative to future relational development. A live alternative is that the first purity is only legal innocence while the focus zakah is exclusively moral character.

changed_reading.before: The replacement is better because the killed youth was already inwardly impure.
changed_reading.after: The replacement is better in prospective growth and family effect, while the killed youth's present purity remains textually live.

context_deltas.mechanism: The explanations distribute desire across a singular speaker, a plural voice, and the Lord, then deny autonomous action from the speaker's own command. In the focus, the plural voices the intervention while the parents' Lord is the grammatical replacing agent, producing a commissioned middle layer rather than an independent preference.

activation_trace.role: Singular intention supplies the first agency position in the explanatory sequence.
Plural intention supplies the focus's intermediate agency position.
Lordship and ownership identify the subject who actually effects the replacement.
The Lord's explicitly attributed intention supplies the final agency position.
Repeated lordship places ultimate authority around both intention and mercy.
Performed action distinguishes enactment from the will authorizing it.
Binding command supplies the authority that the speaker denies originating.

structural_cues: The explanatory triad moves from singular desire in 18:79, to plural desire in 18:81, to the Lord as desiring subject in 18:82, followed by a denial of acting from the speaker's own command.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the pronoun shift, the Lord as subject of replacement, and the disavowal of autonomous command; I infer graded or commissioned agency rather than contradiction. A live alternative is rhetorical variation with no stable hierarchy among the pronouns.

changed_reading.before: The plural speakers independently prefer a replacement and enlist the parents' Lord.
changed_reading.after: The plural voice marks commissioned participation, while the parents' Lord remains the replacing and cultivating agent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The wall explanation presents mercy as guarding a hidden good for dependents until they reach maturity. This temporal protection strengthens the focus's Lord-tended and relational baseline: nearer mercy can describe a family arrangement whose good is preserved to ripen at the fitting time, not only a child's tender disposition.

activation_trace.role: Nurture and completion anchor the focus in developmental guardianship.
Temporal nearness allows the comparative to include approach toward a fitting completion.
Separation from a caregiver creates the vulnerability that guarded mercy answers.
Stored wealth supplies a good whose benefit depends on delayed access.
Reaching an endpoint provides the timetable for release of the protected good.
Attainment of maturity defines the condition at which preservation becomes possession.
Merciful care explicitly names the delayed-guardianship mechanism.

structural_cues: The third explanation links two fatherless children, their righteous father, a concealed inheritance, the Lord's desire, maturation, retrieval, and mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vulnerable children, hidden benefit, a maturity threshold, and explicit mercy; I infer an analogy from protected inheritance to the replacement's protected developmental trajectory. A live alternative is that the third episode concerns property timing only and does not specify the second episode's family bond.

changed_reading.before: Nearer mercy means a replacement child with a kinder temperament.
changed_reading.after: Nearer mercy also names Lordly guardianship that preserves a family's good until it can mature without overwhelming the family.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines a secondary R-B-W mapping under the focus Lord-root with material images of overflow and covering. It remains anchored in the focus Lord-title and zakah specification, but downstream prose should label it a hydraulic cultivation analogy, not a lexical translation of the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Focus words 4 and 7: the Lord-title and zakah specification.

activation_trace.role: Nourishment and organic development let lordly care function as cultivated growth in the analogy.
Increase and flourishing provide the healthy growth that the intervention redirects toward.
Overtaking and covering supply pressure that engulfs the parents.
Overflowing water supplies the cross-domain image of growth exceeding its bounds.
Covering supplies the feared endpoint in which the parents' settled state is submerged.

changed_reading.before: The intervention exchanges a morally worse child for a morally better one.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the intervention reroutes an engulfing overflow into bounded, cultivated growth whose increase can remain near mercy.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the pair-or-even sense of Z-K-W is remote from the ordinary purity and growth readings. It remains anchored in focus word 7, the dual parents, and the focus's kinship terms, with joining and isolation cues elsewhere in the packet; downstream prose should present it only as a structural echo of restored pairing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Focus word 7's rare pair-or-even branch, reinforced by the dual parent pronouns and words 8-9.

activation_trace.role: Pairing and evenness open a rare structural sense for what makes the replacement better.
Kin proximity turns the proposed pairing into a family relation rather than numerical symmetry alone.
Kinship grounds restored pairing in the parents' reciprocal bond.
Joining separated elements supplies the wider packet's recurrent convergence pattern.
A connection maintained between endpoints supplies relational linkage within the convergence pattern.
Isolation without a counterpart supplies the contrasting state that protected pairing answers.

changed_reading.before: Zakah specifies only purity or growth.
changed_reading.after: On a tightly contained branch, zakah also echoes restored pairing: the substitute reknits the two parents into a close family bond.

strongest_changes: The context turns comparative good and zakah from a static moral ranking into a future family trajectory.
The shift from singular to plural to Lord-attributed desire constrains the focus plural as commissioned rather than autonomous agency.
The wall episode expands mercy from temperament into guarded maturation and delayed release of good.
summary.what_was_special: The most productive activation was the collision between present purity in 18:74 and projected parental pressure in 18:80-81. Kinship, womb, temporal nearness, and nurture branches then made the focus comparison relational and developmental, while the overflow and pairing readings remained useful only under explicit containment.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact relation between present purity in 18:74 and zakah in 18:81 may be legal, ethical, developmental, or deliberately multivalent.
The agency progression may encode commission, or it may be rhetorical variation across three explanations.
The final ruhm comparison may privilege compassion, kinship, womb relation, or several of these at once.
